admission.justification: Native held delivery must continue when the old chat-hosting machinery is removed, so sharing that owning path would couple the new guarantee to retired infrastructure.

alternatives.option: Keep native held persistence and delivery independent of hosted-seat/control-plane stores.
alternatives.reason: Native held delivery must continue when the old chat-hosting machinery is removed, so sharing that owning path would couple the new guarantee to retired infrastructure.

alternatives.option: Reuse persisted hosted-seat messaging and its control-plane stores.
alternatives.reason: Reuse would add a caller to machinery the developer decided to remove.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A separately approved hosting boundary is reinstated and demonstrates equivalent native lifetime/permission semantics.

consequences: Native code may share an independent storage primitive but adds no hosted-seat caller; removal belongs to its separately ruled leaf.
context: The earlier hosted-seat message machinery was first proposed for reuse, then marked for removal.

evidence: MIK-R100@v1 rule 4b states that the held-message store does not rest on the product’s own hosting; rule 12 records D126 removal and forbids new hosted-seat callers. This is an authored decision input, not a changed Worker field.
